subject.title: [Bug]: Trajectory files fed back as context cause unbounded token consumption and unexpected API billing

question: Should this issue close based on the shipped trajectory/session guardrails, or stay open until a fresh Windows provider-token proof confirms the billing path is gone?
rationale: Source and release evidence indicate the likely ingestion paths are guarded, but the original impact was real billing across providers and the exact fresh-session workflow has not been re-proven after the guardrails shipped.

options.title: Keep Open For Proof
options.body: Leave this issue open until a maintainer or QA run proves the fresh-session provider-token path with large trajectory sidecars on current main or v2026.6.11.

options.title: Close As Implemented
options.body: Close now if maintainers accept the classifier, memory, TUI, reseed, and trajectory-cap source evidence as sufficient without live billing-path proof.

recommendation.title: Keep Open For Proof
recommendation.body: Leave this issue open until a maintainer or QA run proves the fresh-session provider-token path with large trajectory sidecars on current main or v2026.6.11.

likelyOwner.reason: The central current guardrails and related release verification route through the shared session artifact classifier and release tree that steipete recently touched and discussed.
